title: Quantifying Output Monoculture Using Ecological Diversity Indices

original_idea.title: Quantifying Output Monoculture Using Ecological Diversity Indices
original_idea.problem: No standard diversity metric exists for AI model output ecosystems; current work uses ad hoc similarity scores.
original_idea.direction: Adapt Shannon entropy, Simpson's diversity index, and Rao's quadratic entropy from ecology to measure the diversity of outputs produced by a set of models on a fixed query distribution. Publish a Python library implementing these metrics.
original_idea.why_it_matters: Standardized, interpretable diversity metrics would enable comparable research and allow monitoring of ecosystem diversity over time.
original_idea.relevant_context: Biodiversity literature has decades of validated metrics; ecologists face a structurally identical problem of measuring population monoculture and its risks.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: standardized metrics are a useful infrastructure contribution, but the chain from publishing metrics to improved safety outcomes is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: implementing well-documented ecological indices in Python requires understanding the math but is feasible for CS students with guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: a Python library implementing 3 specific diversity metrics with documentation and examples is concrete and bounded.

novelty.reasoning: Ecological diversity indices (Shannon, Simpson, Rao's quadratic entropy) are well-established in biodiversity literature but have not been systematically adapted and published as a standardized Python library for measuring AI model output diversity. The Artificial Hivemind uses ad hoc similarity scores. No published work provides a formal bridge from ecological diversity metrics to AI output ecosystems with a reusable library. The cross-disciplinary adaptation is mostly novel as a tool contribution.
